newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels blast Colombia pipeline for 43rd time.
newsitem.headline: Rebels blast Colombia pipeline for 43rd time.

text.p: Leftist rebels dynamited one of Colombia's main oil pipelines for the 43rd time this year, halting the pumping of all crude, industry sources said Thursday.
The blast took place Wednesday evening near the town of La Cristalina in northeast Norte de Santander province.

A spokesman for Occidental Petroleum Corp said the pipeline, which runs from the Cano Limon field it operates in northeast Arauca province to the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas should be repaired by late Friday.
"The pipeline has been ruptured an unknown quantity of crude has been spilled," the spokesman said. "But this has not affected production at the field, we're producing fine."
Occidental was forced to shut in its Cano Limon field for eight days earlier this month after back-to-back pipeline bombings, losing more than 1 million barrels of production.
The field is once again producing an average of about 175,000 barrels per day. The pipeline has capacity to pump about 250,000 barrels per day.
Most of the attacks this year have been blamed on the Cuban- inspired National Liberation Army (ELN), the country's second largest rebel force.
Last year the group blasted the pipeline 47 times, according to the state-run oil company Ecopetrol.

In addition to the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline blast, an Ecopetrol spokesman said a smaller pipeline which pumped Cano Limon crude to the Ecopetrol refinery on the Caribbean coast at Cartagena had also been blown up and was currently out of action.
Refining operations have not been affected, however, since the light Cano Limon crude has been substituted with other blends, the Ecopetrol spokesman said.
